zh:
【服问第三十六】

传曰：“有从轻而重，公子之妻为其皇姑。有从重而轻，为妻之父母。有从无服而有服，公子之妻为公子之外兄弟。有从有服而无服，公子为其妻之父母。”传曰：“母出，则为继母之党服；母死，则为其母之党服。为其母之党服，则不为继母之党服。”
三年之丧，既练矣，有期之丧，既葬矣，则带其故葛带，绖期之绖，服其功衰。有大功之丧，亦如之。小功，无变也。
麻之有本者，变三年之葛。既练，遇麻断本者，于免，绖之；既免，去绖。每可以绖必绖；既绖，则去之。
小功不易丧之练冠，如免，则绖其缌小功之绖，因其初葛带。缌之麻，不变小功之葛；小功之麻，不变大功之葛。以有本为税。
殇：长、中，变三年之葛。终殇之月算，而反三年之葛。是非重麻，为其无卒哭之税。下殇则否。
……
en:
【Fu Wen (Mourning Garments) Chapter 36】

The commentary says: "There are cases where one follows a lighter mourning but it becomes heavier, as when the wife of a Shimmer wears mourning for her husband's grandmother. There are cases where one follows a heavier mourning but it becomes lighter, as when one wears mourning for one's wife's parents. There are cases where one who would have no mourning obligation takes on mourning, as when the wife of a Shimmer wears mourning for her husband's cousins on the paternal side. There are cases where one who would have mourning obligations has none, as when a Shimmer wears no mourning for his wife's parents." The commentary says: "If the mother is divorced, then one wears mourning for the kin of the stepmother; if the mother dies, then one wears mourning for the kin of one's own mother. If one wears mourning for the kin of one's own mother, then one does not wear mourning for the kin of the stepmother."
During the three-year mourning, after the first-year sacrifice has been performed, if there occurs a one-year mourning and the burial has already taken place, then one wears the old hempen sash of the original mourning, puts on the mourning headband of the one-year mourning, and wears the coarse mourning garments appropriate to the occasion. If there occurs a nine-month mourning, the same procedure applies. For a five-month mourning, there is no change.
The hempen sash with its roots intact changes the three-year mourning's hempen sash. After the first-year sacrifice, if one encounters mourning requiring the cutting off of the roots of hemp, then at the time of baring the head, one puts on the mourning headband; after the head is bared, one removes the headband. Whenever it is appropriate to put on a headband, one must do so; after putting it on, one then removes it.
For a five-month mourning, one does not change the mourning cap of the three-year mourning after the first-year sacrifice. If one bares the head, then one puts on the headband appropriate to the three-month or five-month mourning, retaining the original hempen sash. The hemp of the three-month mourning does not change the hempen sash of the five-month mourning; the hemp of the five-month mourning does not change the hempen sash of the nine-month mourning. This is because the sash with roots intact is considered more weighty.
For premature deaths: for the elder and middle categories, the three-year mourning's hempen sash is changed. After completing the months of mourning for the premature death, one returns to the three-year mourning's hempen sash. This is not because the hemp is considered more weighty, but because there is no change after the wailing ceremony. For the younger category of premature death, this does not apply.
……

This village is full of gossip, and I've already blended right in. The local kids have a sneaky little operation going, led by a girl named Liu Xiaoping, with her rival, a boy called Zhang Dabao, hot on her heels. And that girl Suqing near the opera stage? Definitely waiting for someone. Heh, I've wandered everywhere. Nothing escapes my notice!

zh:
郑然发现，开封城里的烧火声不见了，那些灼热又难闻的气味也变少了。大家走过街道的时候，怀中钱袋叮叮当当的声音，好像变得更加厚重了。
从什么时候开始的呢……阿然想起来，对了，是那天晚上，有人唱歌的晚上。
有人在唱歌，所以她醒过来，坐在窗边听。
有人在怒吼，所以她朝着声音来的方向探出身，更专注地听。
起风了，叶子刷刷响，才叫回阿然的心神。
然后……然后呢？然后大侠就来啦，街上的叫卖多了，木头的朽味道少了。爹爹回来了！
对了，阿然还没有跟爹爹说过，大侠把金叶子带回来的那天晚上，她做了一个梦呢，梦见——
#Y【金叶子】——一道从心里传出来的声音！阿然应该没听过这句话，但梦里的阿然觉得自己应该是听过的。那个声音说：叶为草编叶，侠为天下人。#E
en:
Zheng Ran noticed that the crackling of fires in Kaifeng City had vanished, and the scorching, acrid smells had faded. When people walked down the streets, the jingle of the coin pouches in their robes sounded somehow fuller and weightier.
When did it begin...? Right, it was that night, the night someone was singing.
That singing woke her, so she sat by the window to listen.
Someone was roaring in anger, so she leaned out toward the sound, listening even more intently.
The wind picked up, and the rustling leaves brought Ran back to her senses.
Then... what happened then? Then the wanderer arrived! The street vendors' cries grew livelier, and the stench of rotting wood faded. Father came home!
Oh, right! Ran still hasn't told Father that on the night the wanderer brought back the gold leaf, she had a dream. She dreamed of...
#Y[The Gold Leaf] A voice echoing from the depths of her heart! Ran shouldn't have known these words, yet in the dream, she felt she had heard them before. The voice said, "The leaf is woven from straw, and a hero is made from the people."#E

zh:
赵光义将唐钱收缴之策的推行全权交给了史判官。
对此，开封府上下并非没有异议，这判官虽有成事之能，却也过于狠厉了些，由他主持此策，恐怕会伤了仁道。众人觉得，是判官的巧言阿谀，抓住了新掌权力的年轻府尹的心。
赵光义并未因此改变心意，战机在即，眼下能够速速成事才是首要的，而在这点上，无人能出判官之右。至于后续安民，待到得胜，朝廷有的是办法。

但他心里依然隐隐感觉到不安，这位判官似乎对自己有一种超乎常理的了解，他的话语常能命中自己的心中所想，仿佛……他就是为着效忠于他而出现的。他无法忽视这种异常，于是他安插了一些耳目到判官身边。
但这些耳目没有带回任何异常的消息。是自己过分多疑，还是这判官比想象中还要手眼通天？
所幸……唐钱收缴即将完成了。
en:
Zhao Guangyi entrusted the entire Tang coin confiscation policy to Magistrate Shi.
This decision was not without dissent in Kaifeng Prefecture. Though the magistrate was capable, his methods were notoriously harsh, so putting him in charge risked undermining the court's benevolent image. Many suspected he'd won over the young prefect with flattery and cunning.
Zhao Guangyi stood firm. With war looming, speed was paramount, and no one matched Magistrate Shi's efficiency in getting results. As for calming public unrest later, victory would provide ample means to mend fences.

Yet a nagging unease lingered. The magistrate seemed to understand him too well, his words often echoing Zhao Guangyi's own unspoken thoughts, as if... he'd been created solely to serve him. Unable to shake this suspicion, Zhao Guangyi planted spies around the magistrate.
But the spies reported nothing unusual. Was he overthinking, or did the magistrate have deeper networks than imagined?
Thankfully... the Tang Coin Confiscation was nearly complete.

zh:
鸿师兄，自你离开已有二十个年头了。途师兄回乡后也再未回过山。
我留在门中，整理机关图册，偶尔闲下来，也教几个小家伙。小家伙有能耐啊，有的利用水力，发明了水运仪象台。有的钻研慈石，探寻以其为动力、以至飞天的可能。
前些日子，有个叫子禹的年轻人，复现了《淮南万毕术》中的试验，还有了些新发现。得巨子青睐，沿袭了你“鸿”的名号。
现在的年轻人，可真了不得。不，应该说，跟你一样，年少时便天资非凡。
不像我，历练半生，才得授名。
如今我身子也不大好了，不知我死后，会是谁继承我的名号呢？
en:
Brant,
It has been twenty years since you left. Senior Brother Tu returned to his hometown and never came back to the mountain.
I stayed in the sect to organize mechanism diagrams. In my spare time, I teach the young ones. They are capable; some used water power to invent the Armillary Sphere. Others study lodestones, exploring their potential for power and even flight.
Recently, a young man named Ziyu reproduced the experiments from The Arts of Ten Thousand Immortals from Huainan and made new discoveries. The Grandmaster favors him, and he has inherited your title, "Brant."
Young people these days are truly remarkable... Or I should say, just like you, they show extraordinary talent from a young age.
Unlike me, who spent half a lifetime training before earning a title.
My health is failing now. I wonder who will inherit my title after I die?

zh:
哀帝禅位朱温，改国号为梁。梁太祖称哀帝温驯，封赏哀帝，迁往曹州。明为封赏，实为发配，举世皆知。
朱温只许哀帝带上少许行囊与侍卫，沿山间小道前往。与从前的天子出行相比，这已然是种羞辱。是以一路上都无人开口说话。
离开王都数十里，有侍卫见一人远远跟在队伍后面，前来禀告李祚。
待侍卫将人带到眼前，李祚才发现此人竟是教坊司教坊使柳青衣。

她跟着车队走了几十里，裙摆上沾了泥渍脏污，一双绣花鞋也开了线。看起来十分窘迫。
李祚别过头去，狠心摆手叫她离开。大约是思及已不是尊贵的天子，不过一条丧家之犬，还有何脸面见她？

复行数十里，一行人寻了处驿站稍作歇息。此地物资匮乏，吃食粗鄙。李祚只吃了一口便不再动筷。
侍卫来报，方才赶走的女子又跟了上来，此时正在驿站外蹲坐着。
此时天色阴沉，此处距离王都又太远，再叫她走回去也不现实，李祚只好唤她进来。

柳青衣比之前见时更加狼狈。李祚并未多言，只叫她坐下吃饭。柳青衣却坐到他的身侧拉起他的手，轻唤“阿祚”。
李祚似是想起从前种种。想到他还是皇子，柳青衣是王都贵女，她的一曲绣金舞超然绝俗。想到柳青衣在树下小声啜泣，诉说对娘亲的思念。想到柳青衣愤愤地说定要让父亲认可自己……
可如今，这些都成了过眼云烟。自己已然不能再护着她。
“青衣，你走吧。”李祚转头望向柳青衣的眼睛。
柳青衣没有回答，她亦望着李祚的眼睛。良久过后，她忽然笑着说：“阿祚，我给你再跳一次绣金舞吧。”

没等李祚回答，柳青衣已兀自起身。
脏污的衣裙无法掩盖绣金舞的风华，一如从前在唐宫中一般。
驿站中的众人皆掩面哭泣。李祚亦不忍。一曲舞毕，两行清泪。
en:
Emperor Ai yielded the throne to Zhu Wen, and the Liang Dynasty was born. Zhu Wen, now Emperor Taizu, praised Ai's "docility," granting him hollow titles and exiling him to Caozhou.
A glorified banishment. Everyone knew it.
Allowed only meager belongings and a handful of guards, the Last Emperor took backroads to his prison. No grand procession, no dignity. The party moved in heavy silence.
A dozen miles from the capital, a guard reported to Li Zuo (the deposed emperor's personal name) a figure trailing them.
When brought forward, Li Zuo froze. It was Liu Qingyi, mistress of the Imperial Entertainment Bureau.

She'd followed for miles, her skirts muddied, embroidered shoes frayed. A pitiful sight.
Li Zuo turned away, waving her off. What right did a fallen emperor, a stray dog, have to face her now?Another stretch of road brought them to a ramshackle courier station. The fare was coarse; Li Zuo took one bite and pushed it aside.
Then the guards whispered: The woman is back, waiting outside the courier station.
Under gathering clouds, too far from the capital to send her away, Li Zuo relented and called her in.

Liu Qingyi looked worse than before. Wordless, he gestured for her to eat. Instead, she sat beside him, took his hand, and murmured, "A'zuo."Memories surged of his princely days, of her as a nobleman's daughter dancing the Aureate Dance with peerless grace. Of her weeping under a tree for a mother's love. Of her vowing to earn her father's pride...Yet the past is the past. Now he could protect nothing, not alone her."Qingyi, leave." He turned around and met her eyes.

Without saying anything, she held his gaze, then suddenly smiled. "A'zuo, let me dance the Aureate Dance for you one last time."
Before he could answer, she stood up.
Mud couldn't dim the Aureate Dance's brilliance. It was just like the palace years.
Every man in the station wept. Li Zuo, too, let silent tears fall as the final pose stilled.

zh:
清河旧地，竹影婆娑。传闻逢雨夜，林中孤井处有青灯泠然，光寒彻骨。有女鬼坐井上，或怅然望月，或嫣然博戏，犹自陶也。
有客夜行于此，见青灯之下一方牌桌，三而缺一。细观之，桌前有两精怪并一绝色女子，眉眼如画，恰如孤魂。
客恍然入寐，鸡鸣方醒，眼前唯有竹影葳蕤。直觉灯芯燃尽，始知非梦。
然某行走世间，未见亡者还魂之事。所谓形骸之所寄，魂魄思念之所在。无名女子做精怪狐语，必有所求。此物不在四方天地之中，而在魂梦交合之处。
客于梦中东行千里，磨心砺骨。而林中唯有一灯，一影，一桌已矣。
en:
On rainy nights, a pale blue lantern glows coldly above a solitary well, where a ghostly woman sits, sometimes gazing longingly at the moon, other times smiling softly as if lost in a quiet game.
A night traveler once passed by and saw a gaming table beneath the lantern light, with one of the four seats empty. Looking closer, two spirits and a peerless beauty sat there, her features as delicate as a painting, appearing like a wandering soul.
The traveler fell into a trance and awoke only at cockcrow to find nothing but lush bamboo shadows. Sensing the wick had burnt to ash, he realized it was no mere dream.
Yet in all my travels, I have never seen the dead return to life. The body is but a vessel, while the soul dwells where its longing lies. This nameless woman, speaking the cryptic tongue of fox spirits, must seek something. It is not found within this world, but at the intersection of soul and dream.
In his dream, the traveler journeyed a thousand miles east, tempering his heart and soul. Yet in the grove, there remained only a lantern, a shadow, and a table.

en:
As the stars shift and the constellations turn, dynasties rise and fall. The Dao of Heaven cannot be altered. Before his physical body and spiritual essence dissipated, Patriarch of Lone Cloud cast his final divination, which foretold the descent of the Vermilion Star to earth a hundred years later to face calamities. Now, just over a century has passed, and rumors have emerged from Roaring Sands Ethereal Mountain that the destined one has appeared on Skyreach Terrace. 
When Emperor Shizong persecuted Buddhism, the Dao sustained all sentient beings. The chanting of scriptures never ceased, and pilgrims came and went without end. What mortals seek is nothing more than fame, fortune, and family harmony. What the Dao calculates is but the self, the human heart, and the Mandate of Heaven. As nobles venerate the deities and perform the Douji ritual (Worship of the Big Dipper), into whose hands does destiny ultimately fall?

The pears used are large, thin-skinned, crisp, and juicy. After being peeled and cored into a jar shape, they are filled with a stuffing of candied tangerine peel, dried longan, wax gourd strips, pitted red dates, hawthorn cake, green plums, and steamed glutinous rice. The pears are then steamed over high heat and finished with a sweet syrup made from sugar, water, and osmanthus paste.

敦煌曲子词指在甘肃敦煌鸣沙山石窟发现的数百首唐五代民间词曲作品，其中包含《云谣集杂曲子》。 
体裁方面，其发现填补了词体在《花间集》定型前的演变空白。在此之前，大多人认为词形成于五代时期，并不知道其实词曲在唐代就已经被广泛地使用。
内容上，敦煌曲子词题材丰富、语言质朴，生动记录了唐五代至宋初敦煌及河西地区的生活场景，尤其展现了多民族共融的珍贵画卷。同时这些词曲内容也修正了早期词作仅有《花间集》等文人作品、多咏男女之情、以婉约为正宗的误解。
en:
Dunhuang Song Lyrics refer to hundreds of folk songs and lyrics works from the Tang and Five Dynasties discovered in the Mogao Grottoes at Mingsha Mountain in Dunhuang, Gansu, including "Collection of Cloud Ballads".  
In terms of genre, their discovery fills the gap in the evolution of ci before it was finalized in Book of Flowers. Prior to this, most people believed that ci formed in the Five Dynasties and were unaware that songs and ci were already widely used in the Tang Dynasty. 
In terms of content, Dunhuang Song Lyrics have rich themes and simple language, vividly recording the life scenes of Dunhuang and the Hexi region from the Tang and Five Dynasties to the early Song Dynasty, especially presenting a precious picture of multi-ethnic integration. At the same time, the content of these songs and lyrics corrects the misunderstanding that early lyrics only included literati works such as Book of Flowers, mostly singing of love between men and women, and taking gracefulness as the orthodox style.

zh:
【经解第二十六】

孔子曰：“入其国，其教可知也。其为人也：温柔敦厚，《诗》教也；疏通知远，《书》教也；广博易良，《乐》教也；洁静精微，《易》教也；恭俭庄敬，《礼》教也；属辞比事，《春秋》教也。故《诗》之失，愚；《书》之失，诬；《乐》之失，奢；《易》之失，贼；《礼》之失，繁；《春秋》之失，乱。其为人也：温柔敦厚而不愚，则深于《诗》者也；疏通知远而不诬，则深于《书》者也；广博易良而不奢，则深于《乐》者也；洁静精微而不贼，则深于《易》者也；恭俭庄敬而不烦，则深于《礼》者也；属辞比事而不乱，则深于《春秋》者也。”
天子者，与天地参。故德配天地，兼利万物，与日月并明，明照四海而不遗微小。其在朝廷，则道仁圣礼义之序；燕处，则听雅、颂之音；行步，则有环佩之声；升车，则有鸾和之音。居处有礼，进退有度，百官得其宜，万事得其序。《诗》云：“淑人君子，其仪不忒。其仪不忒，正是四国。”此之谓也。发号出令而民说，谓之和；上下相亲，谓之仁；民不求其所欲而得之，谓之信；除去天地之害，谓之义。义与信，和与仁，霸王之器也。有治民之意而无其器，则不成。
礼之于正国也：犹衡之于轻重也，绳墨之于曲直也，规矩之于方圜也。故衡诚县，不可欺以轻重；绳墨诚陈，不可欺以曲直；规矩诚设，不可欺以方圆；君子审礼，不可诬以奸诈。是故，隆礼由礼，谓之有方之士；不隆礼、不由礼，谓之无方之民。敬让之道也。故以奉宗庙则敬，以入朝廷则贵贱有位，以处室家则父子亲、兄弟和，以处乡里则长幼有序。孔子曰：“安上治民，莫善于礼。”此之谓也。

en:
【Interpretation of the Classics, No. 26】

Confucius said: "When you enter a state, you can discern its teachings from the people. If the people are gentle and sincere, it is the teaching of the Book of Songs; if they are knowledgeable and far-sighted, it is the teaching of the Book of Documents; if they are broad-minded and easy-going, it is the teaching of Music; if they are pure and subtle, it is the teaching of the Book of Changes; if they are respectful and dignified, it is the teaching of the Book of Rites; if they are skilled in rhetoric and comparison, it is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Therefore, the fault of the Book of Songs lies in foolishness; the fault of the Book of Documents lies in exaggeration; the fault of Music lies in extravagance; the fault of the Book of Changes lies in harm; the fault of the Book of Rites lies in excessive formality; the fault of the Spring and Autumn Annals lies in chaos. If the people are gentle and sincere without being foolish, they have mastered the Book of Songs; if they are knowledgeable and far-sighted without exaggeration, they have mastered the Book of Documents; if they are broad-minded and easy-going without extravagance, they have mastered Music; if they are pure and subtle without harm, they have mastered the Book of Changes; if they are respectful and dignified without excessive formality, they have mastered the Book of Rites; if they are skilled in rhetoric and comparison without chaos, they have mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals."
The Emperor stands alongside Heaven and Earth. Thus, his virtue matches Heaven and Earth, benefits all things, and shines with the brilliance of the Sun and Moon, illuminating all within the four seas without missing even the smallest. In the court, he follows the order of benevolence, sagehood, propriety, and righteousness; in leisure, he listens to the sounds of Elegant and Odes; when walking, he carries the sound of jade rings and pendants; when riding in a carriage, he hears the tones of bells and harmonious instruments. In daily life, he observes propriety; in advancing and retreating, he maintains proper measure; all officials find their appropriate roles, and all matters proceed in proper order. The Book of Songs says: "The virtuous gentleman, his demeanor is without error. His demeanor without error, he corrects the four states." This is what is meant. When orders are issued and the people are pleased, it is called harmony; when superiors and inferiors are close, it is called benevolence; when the people obtain what they desire without seeking it, it is called trustworthiness; when harm to Heaven and Earth is removed, it is called righteousness. Righteousness and trustworthiness, harmony and benevolence—these are the tools of a hegemon or true king. To have the intention of governing the people without these tools cannot succeed.
Propriety in governing a state is like the balance for measuring weight, the ink line for determining straightness, and the compass and square for measuring circles and squares. Therefore, if the balance is truly suspended, one cannot deceive about weight; if the ink line is truly set, one cannot deceive about straightness; if the compass and square are truly established, one cannot deceive about circles and squares; if a gentleman carefully examines propriety, he cannot be deceived by treachery. Thus, honoring propriety and following it is called a person of principle; not honoring propriety and not following it is called a person without principle. This is the way of respect and deference. Therefore, when serving at the ancestral temple, there is reverence; when entering the court, noble and humble have their positions; when in the household, father and son are close, and brothers are harmonious; when in the community, elders and juniors are in proper order. Confucius said: "To secure the ruler and govern the people, nothing is better than propriety." This is what is meant.

zh:
年轻人：
       好久不见，最近过得还好吗？
       托你的福，摊子的生意很好。你阿婶她很久没有这么高兴了，每天笑盈盈地和来往客人唠家常，开心的时候还会借着琵琶摊小娘子的曲子跳上几步！不忙的时候，老张和老幺还张罗着去和赛神队的几个小伙子比赛，哈哈。
      天水集的大伙儿都会提起你，说你行侠仗义，我们听着都很开心，也惦记着你。你阿婶怕你在外面吃不饱穿不暖，时常念叨你呢。有时间就来摊子坐坐啊。
      对了，开烫菜摊子赚了些钱，我们想着也帮衬帮衬别人，就做了些饭菜送给了几个老伙计。怕他们觉得不好意思，我们几个就说，是你要给他们送的。他们还奇怪，说怎么会有没见过的好心人惦记他们呢。老张说这孩子就是这样的，是个热心肠的大侠！他们不太好意思，就给你写了字条，你一起看看吧。
      好了，不说了，待会要来客人了，就到这儿吧。
      希望你一个人在外吃饱穿暖，平平安安。
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6891d7ce5255723325b519a1jb6H0aPM06' size='2290*1296' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Young Hero: 
Long time no see. How have you been? 
Thanks to you, the stall is doing great. Your Auntie hasn't been this happy in ages—she smiles, chatting with customers all day, and even dances a few steps when the Pipa lady plays! When it's slow, Old Zhang and Old Yao even try to race the lads from the deity competition team, haha. 
Everyone at Skybrim Market speaks of your chivalry. We are happy to hear it and miss you often. Your Auntie worries you aren't eating well or staying warm. She talks about you all the time. Come visit the stall when you can. 
Oh, we made some money from the scalding vegetable stall, so we thought we'd help others out. We sent some food to a few old partners. We were afraid they'd feel embarrassed, so we said it was from you. They were surprised a kind hero remembered them! Old Zhang said, "That child is just warm-hearted like that!" They were shy, so they wrote you notes. Take a look. 
Okay, customers are coming. I'll stop here. 
Stay warm, fed, and safe out there.

zh:
未央城有言：人性软弱、恐惧、贪婪等低处，便是商人之财库。因此，时局越动荡，便越能现出商机。

“点检作天子”的预言甚嚣尘上，赵匡胤入主开封只是迟早之事。开封履经变动，百姓听闻又有新主，如同惊弓之鸟，而温无缺却推断赵匡胤极不可能屠城安军。由此，她心生一计——买通无忧帮四散赵匡胤屠城传闻，待到百姓闻风出逃，便低价购入众人资财，待到时局稳定再高价卖出。她本以为如此大赚一笔，不仅能够向救自己的龟奶奶报恩，或许还能重回未央城，却不知恐惧屠城的龟奶奶亦成了她局中之人。
在慌忙变卖了家财的奶奶混乱的话语中，温无缺逐渐明白，龟奶奶的女儿就死在上一次屠城之中，无法承受孩子全部离开了自己的她，开始变得有点疯疯癫癫的，见着年轻女孩，便要当做自己的盈盈……直到救下了浑身伤痕的自己，她那时的样子，实在太像盈盈最后的样子。奶奶哭得声嘶力竭，温无缺为了安抚她，只得暂且与她出城。那一天开封下了雪，站在那些流离失所，满身脏污、争打不休的难民中间，她终于看到了“财库”这个词背后血淋淋的图景。

她忽然想到很久以前的一桩事，她驾着黄金的马车走在未央城外的大道上，随手将赌输了的一枚玉玦掷下时，就仿佛向水池里投下了鱼食一般，一群蓬头垢面的人围上来，互相撕打着争夺，那时，她与华服的侍从笑他们的样子倒像是恶犬。
仓廪实而知礼节，笑恶犬，饥饿时谁非恶犬？如此想来，一生为利从商，实在罪大恶极。

温无缺日渐消瘦了下去，若是重回未央城，也不过重蹈那鲜血淋漓的覆辙……她感觉自己身上失去了往日的力气。她拖着伤病的身子，每日只是按部就班地陪龟奶奶到街上去卖些小手艺，本以为余生便就此了结。可渐渐地，她竟然从那些小贩身上，看到了另一种为商的可能。
小贩日夜辛劳，虽是为了自己之利，却也是为了与人为利，人人皆有所需，商人可使无者有，使远者近，使缓者速，与其说商人是在伤害人，倒不如说商人是在帮助人。以前总觉得需要制造问题方能获利，可放眼一看，世间本就有很多问题亟待解决。

她渐渐有了活力，后来，她还破天荒地救下了一只伤痕累累的小猫。
以前总觉得与人争斗其乐无穷，却不知为善亦有乐趣，龟奶奶喜见她因着小猫脸上渐渐有了笑意，也对着夜灯，为盈盈做了一顶猫儿般的帽子，帽子上连着编织的黑发辫子，戴上这帽子，盈盈出门卖货，便不会因金发惹人侧目。
东阙公子成了角门里人见人爱的嘴甜小货娘，虽是清贫些，但也颇有乐趣，温无缺有时候想，此生若能如此，倒也足矣。

然而乱世未尽，人心不足，好景亦不能长久。唐钱收缴之策兴，想要维持住清贫祥和的日子，也成了奢望。
这世道不该如此，温无缺想。
于是在一个晴夜，温无缺枕在龟奶奶的腿上说，她要离家一趟。
“我要去做一笔顶大的生意。”
en:
In Weiyang City, it is said: The weaknesses of humanity, vulnerability, fear and greed, are a merchant's treasury. Thus, the more turbulent the times, the greater the opportunity.

As rumors of "The Military Inspector Shall Be Emperor" spread, it was only a matter of time before Zhao Kuangyin seized Kaifeng. The city's residents, traumatized by repeated upheavals, panicked at the news of a new ruler. But Wen Wuque deduced that Zhao Kuangyin was unlikely to massacre the city to assert power. She hatched a plan: bribe the Unbound Cavern to spread rumors of an impending massacre, then buy up citizens' assets at rock-bottom prices as they fled, only to resell them at a premium when order returned. She believed this windfall would let her repay Granny Turtle, who'd saved her, and perhaps even reclaim her place in Weiyang City. What she didn't know was that Granny Turtle, terrified of another massacre, would become a pawn in her own scheme.
As Granny Turtle frantically sold her possessions, her disjointed words revealed the truth: her daughter had died in the last massacre. Unable to bear the loss of her children, she had grown delusional, treating every young girl as her "Yingying", until she'd found Wen Wuque, bloodied and broken, resembling her daughter in her final moments. As Granny Turtle sobbed uncontrollably, Wen Wuque could only pacify her by fleeing the city with her. That day, Kaifeng snowed. Standing among the filthy, desperate refugees fighting over scraps, Wen Wuque finally saw the bloody reality behind the term "merchant's treasury".

She recalled a distant memory: riding in a golden wagon outside Weiyang City, she'd tossed a lost jade pendant into the crowd. Like feeding fish, it had sparked a brutal scramble among ragged beggars, which she and her servants had laughed at, calling them "vicious hounds." 
Only when the granaries are full do people observe morality. But in hunger, who is not a vicious hound? She realized her life of profit-driven commerce had been a litany of sins.

Wen Wuque wasted away. Returning to Weiyang City would only lead to more bloodshed, she felt her old ambition draining away. Dragging her injured body, she accompanied Granny Turtle daily to sell trinkets on the street, resigning herself to a quiet end. But gradually, she saw a different kind of commerce in the hawkers around her. 
They toiled both for their own gain and to meet others' needs. Merchants could bridge gaps, bringing goods to those who lacked them, smoothing supply and demand. Perhaps they aided people more than exploited them. She'd always thought profit required creating problems, but the world was full of genuine needs waiting to be solved.
Her vitality returned, and she even saved a scarred stray cat.
Once obsessed with conquest, she now found joy in kindness. Granny Turtle, delighted by her smiles, knitted a cap with cat ears and attached braids, so "Yingying" could sell her wares without drawing stares for her golden hair.
The Ember of East became a beloved peddler in Forsaken Quarter, poor, but content. This life could be enough, Wen Wuque sometimes thought.

But chaos endures, and human greed never sleeps. When the Tang Dynasty's coin confiscation policies began, even a simple, peaceful life became a luxury.
The world should not be like this, Wen Wuque thought.
One clear night, resting on Granny Turtle's lap, she announced she must leave.
"I'm going to make the biggest deal of my life."

zh:
【宣公第七】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。公子遂如齐逆女。
继弑君不言即位，此其言即位何？其意也。
〇三月，遂以夫人妇姜至自齐。
遂何以不称公子？一事而再见者，卒名也。夫人何以不称姜氏？贬。曷为贬？讥丧娶也。丧娶者，公也，则曷为贬夫人？内无贬于公之道也。内无贬于公之道，则曷为贬夫人？夫人与公一体也。其称妇何？有姑之辞也。
〇夏，季孙行父如齐。
〇晋放其大夫胥甲父于卫。
放之者何？犹曰无去是云尔。然则何言尔？近正也。此其为近正奈何？古者大夫已去，三年待放。君放之，非也；大夫待放，正也。古者臣有大丧，则君三年不呼其门已练，可以弁冕服金革之事。君使之，非也；臣行之，礼也。闵子要绖而服事，既而曰："若此乎，古之道不即人心。"退而致仕，孔子盖善之也。
〇公会齐侯于平州。
〇公子遂如齐。
〇六月，齐人取济西田。
外取邑不书，此何以书？所以赂齐也。曷为赂齐？为弑子赤之赂也。
〇秋，邾娄子来朝。
〇楚子、郑人侵陈，遂侵宋。
〇晋赵盾帅师救陈。宋公、陈侯、卫侯、曹伯会晋师于斐林，伐郑。
此晋赵盾之师也，曷为不言赵盾之师？君不会大夫之辞也。
〇冬，晋赵穿帅师侵柳。
柳者何？天子之邑也。曷为不系乎周？不与伐天子也。
〇晋人、宋人伐郑。

二年，春，王二月壬子，宋华元帅师及郑公子归生帅师，战于大棘。宋师败绩，获宋华元。
〇秦师伐晋。
〇夏，晋人、宋人、卫人、陈人侵郑。
〇秋九月乙丑，晋赵盾弑其君夷嗥。
〇冬十月乙亥，天王崩。

……
en:
【Duke Xuan, Volume Seven】

First Year, Spring, the King's first month, the Duke assumed the throne. Prince Su went to Qi to welcome the bride.
Following the assassination of a ruler, one does not announce the succession. Why does this text announce it? Because it was his intention.
〇In the third month, Su brought the Lady, born of the Jiang clan, back from Qi.
Why is Su not called Prince? When the same person appears twice in one matter, the final mention uses his personal name. Why is the Lady not called Jiang? To censure her. Why censure? To criticize marrying during mourning. The one marrying during mourning was the Duke, so why censure the Lady? Within the state, there is no way to censure the Duke. Since there is no way to censure the Duke, why censure the Lady? The Lady and the Duke are one body. Why is she called "the bride"? This is the term used when a mother-in-law is still alive.
〇In Summer, Jisun Xingfu went to Qi.
〇Jin exiled its Grand Master Xu Jiafu to Wei.
What does "exile" mean? It is like saying "do not leave this place." Then why mention it? Because it is close to correct. How is it close to correct? In ancient times, when a Grand Master had already left, he waited three years for permission to be exiled. If the ruler exiled him, that was wrong; if the Grand Master waited for exile, that was correct. In ancient times, when a minister had a great mourning, the ruler would not summon him to his gate for three years. After the mourning garments were removed, he could wear the cap and robes and serve in military matters. If the ruler made him serve, that was wrong; if the minister served, that was proper. Minzi wore the mourning sash and served, then said: "Is this how it is? The ancient way does not suit the human heart." He withdrew and retired from office. Confucius approved of this.
〇The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Pingzhou.
〇Prince Su went to Qi.
〇In the sixth month, the people of Qi took the fields west of Ji.
When another state takes a city, it is not recorded. Why is this recorded? Because it was a bribe to Qi. Why bribe Qi? It was a bribe for the assassination of Zi Chi.
〇In Autumn, the Viscount of Zhulou came to court.
〇The Viscount of Chu and the people of Zheng invaded Chen, then invaded Song.
〇Zhao Dun of Jin led troops to rescue Chen. The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met with the Jin army at Feilin to attack Zheng.
This was Zhao Dun's army, so why is it not called Zhao Dun's army? It is the wording for when a ruler does not meet with a Grand Master.
〇In Winter, Zhao Chuan of Jin led troops to invade Liu.
What is Liu? It is the King's city. Why is it not attached to Zhou? Because it does not approve of attacking the Son of Heaven.
〇The people of Jin and the people of Song attacked Zheng.

Second Year, Spring, the King's second month, on Renzi day, Hua Yuan of Song led troops and Prince Guisheng of Zheng led troops, and they fought at Daji. The Song army was defeated, and Hua Yuan of Song was captured.
〇The Qin army attacked Jin.
〇In Summer, the people of Jin, Song, Wei, and Chen invaded Zheng.
〇In Autumn, the ninth month, on Yichou day, Zhao Dun of Jin assassinated his ruler, Yihao.
〇In Winter, the tenth month, on Yihai day, the King of Heaven passed away.

……

The day Feng Yi drank the Cornus Soup, that person placed a bloodstained jade pendant in his palm.
"Tsk, look at this red jade... such strong killing intent. Silver Needle saves lives, so why are you the only one who kills?"
"Sometimes, killing is necessary to save lives." 
"...I don't understand."
"Now you carry the pendant. The bloodstain will fade, or it will grow—it depends on your choice."
It was only long after that Feng Yi came to understand: the one called the Red-Sleeved Immortal could never see the Red Sleeve Disc again.
The blood upon the jade reflects the world, and it was never his to decide.

Even now, it refuses to rest.
Let it drink deeply of ink, carving yet another stroke into the annals of history.

zh: 学术无界，文津馆常邀约天下名士大儒前来闻道堂传道授业，其中不乏多朝官吏。但文津馆学子一旦踏入官场，则视为肄业，此后不再算作本门中人。此规看似不近人情，但颇为周全。唐末国土分崩，多朝并立，学子们自可各为其主，文津馆绝不入局，如此才可保文脉绵延，留下一线生机。
en: Learning knows no bounds, and the Inkbound Order often extends invitations to renowned scholars from across the realm to come to Wendao Hall and teach. Among them are quite a few government officials of various courts. Yet should any student of the Inkbound Order set foot upon the path of officialdom, they are considered to have left their studies incomplete, and are no longer counted among those of the Order. The rule may seem wanting in compassion, yet it is in truth a most prudent measure. As the Tang fell and the realm shattered into many courts, students were free to serve whichever lord they chose, but the Inkbound Order would not be drawn into any faction. Only thus could the cultural lineage be kept unbroken, and a thread of hope preserved.

【一】

天地玄黄，宇宙洪荒。
日月盈昃，辰宿列张。
寒来暑往，秋收冬藏。
闰余成岁，律吕调阳。
云腾致雨，露结为霜。
金生丽水，玉出昆冈。
剑号巨阙，珠称夜光。
果珍李柰，菜重芥姜。
海咸河淡，鳞潜羽翔。
龙师火帝，鸟官人皇。
始制文字，乃服衣裳。
推位让国，有虞陶唐。
吊民伐罪，周发殷汤。
坐朝问道，垂拱平章。
爱育黎首，臣伏戎羌。
遐迩一体，率宾归王。
鸣凤在竹，白驹食场。
化被草木，赖及万方。
盖此身发，四大五常。
恭惟鞠养，岂敢毁伤。
女慕贞洁，男效才良。
知过必改，得能莫忘。
罔谈彼短，靡恃己长。
信使可覆，器欲难量。
墨悲丝染，诗赞羔羊。
景行维贤，克念作圣。
德建名立，形端表正。
空谷传声，虚堂习听。
祸因恶积，福缘善庆。
尺璧非宝，寸阴是竞。
资父事君，曰严与敬。
孝当竭力，忠则尽命。
临深履薄，夙兴温凊。
似兰斯馨，如松之盛。
川流不息，渊澄取映。
容止若思，言辞安定。
笃初诚美，慎终宜令。
荣业所基，籍甚无竟。
学优登仕，摄职从政。
存以甘棠，去而益咏。
乐殊贵贱，礼别尊卑。
上和下睦，夫唱妇随。
en:
[I]


Heaven is dark, yellow is the earth; a vast primordial void before the cosmos' birth.
The sun and moon wax and wane; the stars are spread across the sky.
Cold arrives then heat once more; Autumn's harvest, Winter's store.
Extra days round out the years; scale in tune with sun and spheres.
Clouds soar up to end in rain; the dew congeals to morning frost.
Gold is born in the River Li; jade comes from Kunlun's vault.
A sword is styled "Juque"; a pearl, the "Gleam of Night."
Dearest fruit are pears and apples; fine crops mustard, ginger.
Sea is saline, streams sublime; fish school below, birds flock on high.
Dragon Master, Fire King; Bird Officer, Lord of Men.
Writing was invented, and garments were worn.
Yielding the throne, passing the land; rulers of Yu, Tao and Tang.
Relieve the people, right the wrong; as did Zhou's Fa, as did Yin's Tang.
Presiding at court and asking the Way; gracious yet lordly, discuss and decide.
With love he taught the common folk; in submission, wild tribes.
Far and near, they joined as one; all followed, rallied to the king.
The phoenix calls from bamboo stand; White pony grazes pasture land.
Wise teachings dress each plant and tree; bounty everywhere we see.
These bodies and this hair of ours; Four Great Things, Five Principles.
Do honor to my parents' upbringing; how dare I bring myself to hurt?
Women should admire chastity and purity; men should emulate talent and virtue.
Correct your errors to set them right; keep your mastered skills forever in sight.
Do not gossip about others' faults; do not boast of your own strengths.
A trustworthy messenger's word can be verified; a vessel's capacity should be hard to measure.
Mozi lamented that white silk could be dyed any color; the Book of Odes praises the lamb.
Admiring the virtuous inspires emulation; mastering one's thoughts leads to sagehood.
When virtue is established, one's name is made; when form is upright, one's bearing is correct.
A sound echoes through the empty valley; a whisper is heard clearly in an empty hall.
Misfortune stems from accumulated evil; fortune comes from accumulated good deeds.
A foot of jade is not treasure; an inch of time is worth contesting for.
To serve one's father and one's lord is to show solemnity and reverence.
Filial piety requires utmost effort; loyalty demands one's very life.
Tread as by a deep abyss or on thin ice; rise early to tend your parents with warmth and coolness in season.
Fragrant like the orchid, flourishing like the pine.
The river flows endlessly; the deep pool reflects clearly.
Composure as if in thought, words calm and steady.
To be true at the beginning is a virtue; to be careful through the end is a mark of honor.
These virtues form the foundation of honorable endeavors, leading to boundless and enduring renown.
Those who excel in learning may enter office and take up the duties of governance.
His memory lives on like the sweet pear tree left behind; the more he is gone, the more he is praised in song.
Music differs by rank; rites differ by status.
Above, harmony; below, concord - husband leads, wife follows.
Continue to uncover the truth

zh:
雪儿是夫子最喜欢的那种好学生。
上课永远坐在最前面，脊背挺得笔直；功课从来做得最认真，字迹端正，整整齐齐。
但雪儿没有朋友，大家都不喜欢和她玩，说她较真，说她无趣。
她才不在意。她要多读些书，多做些算经，多背些图纸，才能考入内门，当上大匠。
只是……只是偶尔从书本里抬起头时，也会想，墨城外面是什么样子的呢？
她娘总说，外面危险。她长这么大，最远也只是跟着娘去旧址，拜祭她爹。
那碑刻斑驳，风一吹，像有人低语。
娘会指着那些小小的匣子，一个一个念：“这是你爷爷，这是你伯伯，这是你爹……他是出山给人修桥的时候走的。”
雪儿只觉得肩膀上沉沉的。
所以当夫子说，有两个从碧水云涛来的小娃，让雪儿帮忙带着玩的时候，雪儿很开心。
她都想好了——若是女娃，就一起做木鸢，若是男娃，就送他们尚贤书店最新的书册。
可从碧水云涛来的小粟和小米，一个拼个木鸢都要三天；另一个把《千字文》折成纸鹊，嗖地一下飞出窗外，还哈哈大笑。
雪儿心里急说话也急：“你们这样考不进内门，当不了大匠怎么办？”
小米一边叠纸鹊一边说，头也不抬：“那就不做什么大匠，我们做少年三杰！”
“少年三杰？”雪儿愣住，“那是什么？”
“就是我们仨啊！”小米扬手，纸鹊乘风而起，飞出窗外，“不靠别人，自己闯出来的名号！”
“那……要当三杰有什么要求呀？”雪儿迟疑地问。
小米也被问住了，挠挠头：“小粟你说，少年三杰是什么要求？”
小粟听见问话，慢悠悠抬起头：“大概是……鸦先生那么厉害吧。”
雪儿笑了：“鸦先生是谁，有多厉害呀，比巨子还厉害吗？”
“现在的巨子都是鸦先生的徒弟，当然是鸦先生厉害。”小米眨眨眼。
“你们又说大话。我不信……那你们是鸦先生的弟子，怎么连小考都不如我。”雪儿摇头。
“区区小考而已，我们才不学那些！”小米站起来，“你敢不敢和我比机关术？”
“怎么不敢！”她脱口而出，然后输了个彻底。
“鸦先生说了，只读书，读死书。以后，我教你机关术，你教我认字。”小米抹了抹鼻子。
……
雪儿坐在机关牛背上，看着远处墨城的影子越来越远，像一座未起飞的木鸢。
她想，等她去碧水云涛看看，再回来决定是做少年三杰还是做墨门大匠，也不迟。
en:
Xue was the pride and joy of the schoolmaster. In every lesson, she sat in the very front row, her back straight as an arrow. She always took her coursework seriously, keeping her handwriting perfectly neat and orderly.
But Xue had no friends. The other children didn't like playing with her, calling her a stickler and a bore. She didn't care. She just needed to read more books, solve more equations, and memorize more blueprints. Only then could she pass into the Inner Sect and become a Grand Artisan.
Yet... whenever she stole a quiet moment away from her books, she couldn't help but wonder what life beyond Mohist City looked like.

"The world outside is dangerous," her mother always warned.
The farthest Xue had ever traveled was to the Old City, where they went to pay respects to her father. The stone tablets were weathered and mottled. When the wind blew, they sounded like someone whispering. Her mother would point to the row of small boxes, reciting the names one by one.
"This is your grandfather, this is your uncle, and this is your father... He passed away when he left to build a bridge for people."
Xue only felt a heavy weight on her young shoulders.

So when the schoolmaster asked her to look after two kids from Jadestream Valley, Xue was thrilled. She had it all planned out. If they were girls, they would build wooden eagles together. If they were boys, she would give them the latest books from the Shangxian Bookstore.
However, Su and Mi from Jadestream Valley were so very different. One took three whole days just to assemble a single wooden eagle. The other folded his textbook into a paper crane, sending it soaring out the window with a whoosh while laughing out loud.

Xue grew anxious, her words tumbling out. "If you keep this up, you'll never get into the Inner Sect! What will you do if you can't become Grand Artisans?"
Mi didn't even look up from folding his paper crane. "Then we won't be Grand Artisans. We'll be the Three Junior Paragons!"
"The Three Junior Paragons?" Xue froze. "What's that?"
"That's the three of us!" Mi tossed his hand up, letting the paper crane catch the breeze and fly out the window. "A title we'll make for ourselves without relying on anyone else!"

"So... what does it take to be the Three Junior Paragons?" Xue asked hesitantly.
Mi was stumped. He scratched his head. "Hey Su, what does it take to be the Three Junior Paragons?"
Su slowly looked up at the question. "Probably... being as amazing as Master Raven."
Xue smiled. "Who is Master Raven? How amazing is he? Is he even greater than the Grandmaster?"
"The Grandmasters of today are all Master Raven's disciples. Of course he's the greatest." Mi blinked at her.

"You're just bragging again. I don't believe a word of it... If you're really his disciples, why are your quiz scores worse than mine?" Xue shook her head.
"It's just a silly little quiz. We don't bother studying that stuff!" Mi stood up proudly. "Dare to challenge me in mechanics?"
"You're on!" she blurted out, only to lose spectacularly.
"Master Raven always said studying all the time makes you rigid. Tell you what, I'll teach you mechanics, and you teach me how to read," Mi said, rubbing his nose.

...

Sitting atop the mechanical ox, Xue watched the silhouette of Mohist City fade into the distance. From afar, it looked like a wooden eagle waiting to take flight.
She thought it wouldn't be too late to decide her path after visiting Jadestream Valley. Whether she became one of the Three Junior Paragons or a great Mohist artisan, there was still plenty of time.

zh:
在很早很早以前，阿依奴还是一个和葡萄苗差不多高的小姑娘。
她总爱趁阿爸不注意，溜到邻家葡萄园门口，眨巴着圆溜溜的眼睛，软乎乎地喊："婶婶~葡萄好香呀~可不可以给我尝尝~"
这招从未失手，阿依奴总能要到一颗又大又甜的葡萄。
 
可每次被阿爸逮着都要挨骂。
周围人都劝："哎呀，少颗葡萄能咋样？小阿依奴又是捶肩又是揉腿的，哄得我们多栽两株葡萄也情愿哩！"
阿爸却板着脸——葡萄是庄户人家的命根子，不是甜甜的零嘴，怎么能随便找人讨要！"实在馋了...吃自家葡萄不成么？莫非阿爸种的葡萄不甜？"
"才不是！"阿依奴小声反驳，阿爸的葡萄最厉害的。可……可阿爸哥哥整夜整夜守着葡萄藤酿酒，她看到自家葡萄就觉得是汗水的味道，很苦很苦。
阿爸听了无可奈何，和大家道了歉，默默把阿依奴牵回了家。
 
第二天，阿依奴揉着眼睛推开窗，她发现家门口旁新移栽了一小株葡萄！——这是专为她栽的，不酿酒的家葡萄。
从此，阿依奴每天睡前都要去数数藤上葡萄，算着着明早醒来，藤上能成熟几颗。如果熟了一颗自己吃，两颗分哥哥，三颗……四颗……就可以阿爸、哥哥和阿依奴一人一颗，还要埋在土里一颗，给阿妈吃！这是独属于一家人的甜蜜。

家门口那株小小的葡萄藤，后来去哪里了呢？后来不见了。
en:
Long, long ago, Aynur was still a little girl about as tall as a grapevine seedling. 
She loved to sneak to the entrance of the neighbor's vineyard when Father wasn't looking, blink her round eyes, and ask softly, "Auntie... the grapes smell so good... could you give me one to taste?" 
This trick never failed. Aynur always got a big, sweet grape. 
 
But every time Father caught her, she'd get scolded. 
The people around persuaded him: "Ah, what's the harm in losing one grape? Little Aynur beats our shoulders and rubs our legs, we'd even plant two more grapevines just to make her happy!" 
But her father frowned, grapes were the lifeblood of farmer families, not sweet snacks. How could she ask others for them casually? "If you're really craving... can't you eat our own grapes? Are the grapes your father grows not sweet enough?" 
"That's not it!" Aynur would whisper in protest, Father's grapes are the best. But... but Father and Brother guarded the grapevines all night making wine, whenever she saw their grapes, she thought they tasted of sweat, very bitter. 
Hearing this, Father could only sigh helplessly, apologized to everyone, and silently led Aynur back home. 
 
The next day, Aynur rubbed her eyes and pushed open the window to find a small, newly transplanted grapevine by their doorstep! This was a home grapevine planted just for her, not for making wine. 
From then on, Aynur would count the grapes on the vine every night before bed, calculating how many might ripen by morning. If one ripened, she'd eat it herself; if two, she'd share one with Brother; if three... four... then Father, Brother, and Aynur could each have one, and she'd bury one in the soil for Mother! This was a sweetness belonging solely to the family. 

That little grapevine by the doorstep, where did it go later? Later, it was gone.
Outsider! What are you doing here?

傅千里是王清从雪地里捡回来的孤儿，因是女儿身，后交由沈寒英抚养授艺。
傅千里跟着她学，练刀最勤，处事最周，就连那严酷的样子，也学去了九成了，冷冽似霜雪。渐渐地，成了同门心中那道沉默而可靠的身影。
中渡桥的消息传来时，她看见师父独立院中，望着北方出神，指节在刀柄上紧了又松。
若心有牵绊，刀便有了犹豫。
傅千里懂。
当夜，她取走师父惯用的横刀，留书一行：“霜雪可代寒英落，此桥当由千里赴。” 
天未亮，人已远。肩上所负，只比刀更沉。
en:
Fu Qianli was an orphan Wang Qing rescued from the snow. Because she was a girl, she was later given to Shen Hanying to be raised and trained.
Fu Qianli studied under her, practicing the blade most diligently and handling matters most thoroughly. She even learned ninety percent of that stern demeanor, cold as frost and snow. Gradually, she became that silent, reliable figure in the hearts of her peers.
When news from Zhongdu Bridge arrived, she saw her master standing alone in the courtyard, staring toward the north, her knuckles tightening and loosening on her sword hilt.
If the heart is tethered, the blade will hesitate.
Fu Qianli understood.
That night, she took her master's usual Heng Blade and left a single line: "Frost and snow can fall in place of the flower; this bridge should be crossed by the one from a thousand miles."
The person was gone before dawn. The burden on her shoulders was heavier than the blade.

仙人猫也不清楚自己是怎么走到今天的。
它原本是家中最小的那个，但那场它无法理解的火，让它变成了家中仅剩的一个。
它失去了一切，只拥有了传说中无价的自由。
对这可憎的世间它可没什么好脾性，在做噩梦的夜晚更是会发出凄厉的叫声。偏偏是这声声惨叫——据说曾救下过许多在大漠中因为打了瞌睡险些被野兽袭击的旅人。
因此，越来越多人传它是只救人性命的仙人猫。
那些活下来的人回来了，都想要摸一摸这只仙人猫。可它见人就凶，任谁都难近它一步。
越是这样，人们越想讨它欢心。就这样，越来越多奉它为主的人出现了……
仙人猫有时候会想，这些人，不，这些“仆从”，算是它的家人吗？
还是说它的家人，其实换了一种方式回来了？
仙人猫才不承认自己需要这些人，它仍在夜晚凄厉地叫着
——只不过，也许不再是因为频繁的噩梦了。
en:
The Cat-ismatic Immortal doesn't quite understand how it got here.
It was once the smallest in its family. Then came the fire, an incomprehensible cruelty that left it the only one. It lost everything. In return, it gained the freedom spoken of only in legends.
It holds no kindness for this wretched world. On nights haunted by recurring nightmares, it lets out piercing, mournful cries—cries that have, ironically, saved countless desert travelers from wild beasts as they dozed on the sands.
Because of this, many see it as a guardian spirit: the Cat-ismatic Immortal. Survivors return, hoping for a single touch, but it meets every approach with a snarl, keeping all at bay. Yet, the more it withdraws, the more devoted they become, until a following forms to worship it as a master.
Sometimes, the Cat-ismatic Immortal wonders: are these "servants" its family? Or has its family returned in some new form?
It won't admit needing them. It still howls through the night.
But perhaps now, it's no longer from the nightmares.

一柄外观粗粝的小剑，可做些简单的伸缩变化。
因师长多年在外游历，青、鸦所学，实多承于张万师。
彼时青年幼贪玩，课业之事，全不上心，草以此剑作课绩交上。鸦看此物实在敷衍，怕惹得师兄张万师生气，便想助青重做。奈何时日蹙迫，仓促间鸦只能胡乱在剑中再补一飞针机括。
后张万师品评此剑，称以青、鸦二人年纪，做一柄孩童把玩之物，倒也适宜，颇有童趣。青、鸦羞赧无言，此后课绩，再未做出师兄口中的“童趣”之物。
张万师暗中懊恼许久，将此“孤品”小心珍藏。
en:
A rough-looking small sword capable of simple extension and retraction.
As their master traveled for years, what Halcyon and Raven learned was largely inherited from Zhang Wanshi.
At the time, Halcyon was young and playful, caring little for his studies, and hastily submitted this sword as his assignment. Raven saw how perfunctory it was and, fearing it would anger their senior brother Zhang Wanshi, wanted to help Halcyon redo it. However, time was short; in his haste, Raven could only clumsily add a flying needle to the sword.
Later, when Zhang Wanshi evaluated the sword, he remarked that for Halcyon and Raven's age, making a child's plaything was actually fitting and quite whimsical. Halcyon and Raven were too ashamed to speak, and from then on, their assignments never again featured the "whimsy" their senior brother spoke of.
Zhang Wanshi secretly regretted his comment for a long time, yet he carefully treasured this "one-of-a-kind" piece.

zh:
【表记第三十二】

子言之：“归乎！君子隐而显，不矜而庄，不厉而威，不言而信。”子曰：“君子不失足于人，不失色于人，不失口于人，是故君子貌足畏也，色足惮也，言足信也。《甫刑》曰：‘敬忌而罔有择言在躬。’”子曰：“裼袭之不相因也，欲民之毋相渎也。”子曰：“祭极敬，不继之以乐；朝极辨，不继之以倦。”子曰：“君子慎以辟祸，笃以不掩，恭以远耻。”子曰：“君子庄敬日强，安肆日偷。君子不以一日使其躬儳焉，如不终日。”子曰：“齐戒以事鬼神，择日月以见君，恐民之不敬也。”子曰：“狎侮，死焉而不畏也。”子曰：“无辞不相接也，无礼不相见也；欲民之毋相亵也。《易》曰：‘初筮告，再三渎，渎则不告。’”
子言之：“仁者，天下之表也；义者，天下之制也；报者，天下之利也。”子曰：“以德报德，则民有所劝；以怨报怨，则民有所惩。《诗》曰：‘无言不雠，无德不报。’《太甲》曰：‘民非后无能胥以宁；后非民无以辟四方。’”子曰：“以德报怨，则宽身之仁也；以怨报德，则刑戮之民也。”子曰：“无欲而好仁者，无畏而恶不仁者，天下一人而已矣。是故君子议道自己，而置法以民。”子曰：“仁有三，与仁同功而异情。与仁同功，其仁未可知也；与仁同过，然后其仁可知也。仁者安仁，知者利仁，畏罪者强仁。仁者右也，道者左也。仁者人也，道者义也。厚于仁者薄于义，亲而不尊；厚于义者薄于仁，尊而不亲。道有至、有义、有考。至道以王，义道以霸，考道以为无失。”
子言之：“仁有数，义有长短小大。中心憯怛，爱人之仁也；率法而强之，资仁者也。《诗》云：‘丰水有芑，武王岂不仕！诒厥孙谋，以燕翼子，武王烝哉！’数世之仁也。国风曰：‘我今不阅，皇恤我后。’终身之仁也。”子曰：“仁之为器重，其为道远，举者莫能胜也，行者莫能致也，取数多者仁也；夫勉于仁者不亦难乎？是故君子以义度人，则难为人；以人望人，则贤者可知已矣。”子曰：“中心安仁者，天下一人而已矣。大雅曰：‘德輶如毛，民鲜克举之；我仪图之，惟仲山甫举之，爱莫助之。’”小雅曰：“高山仰止，景行行止。”子曰：“《诗》之好仁如此；乡道而行，中道而废，忘身之老也，不知年数之不足，俛焉日有孳孳，毙而后已。”子曰：“仁之难成久矣！人人失其所好；故仁者之过易辞也。”子曰：“恭近礼，俭近仁，信近情，敬让以行此，虽有过，其不甚矣。夫恭寡过，情可信，俭易容也；以此失之者，不亦鲜乎？《诗》曰：‘温温恭人，惟德之基。’”子曰：“仁之难成久矣，惟君子能之。是故君子不以其所能者病人，不以人之所不能者愧人。是故圣人之制行也，不制以己，使民有所劝勉愧耻，以行其言。礼以节之，信以结之，容貌以文之，衣服以移之，朋友以极之，欲民之有壹也。小雅曰：‘不愧于人，不畏于天。’是故君子服其服，则文以君子之容；有其容，则文以君子之辞；遂其辞，则实以君子之德。是故君子耻服其服而无其容，耻有其容而无其辞，耻有其辞而无其德，耻有其德而无其行。是故君子衰绖则有哀色；端冕则有敬色；甲胄则有不可辱之色。《诗》云：‘惟鹈在梁，不濡其翼；彼记之子，不称其服。’”
……
en:
【Biaoji Thirty-Second】

The Master said: "Return! The gentleman remains hidden yet becomes manifest; without being stern, he is dignified; without being severe, he inspires awe; without speaking, he is trusted." The Master said: "The gentleman does not err in his steps before others, does not err in his countenance before others, does not err in his words before others. Therefore, the gentleman's appearance is sufficient to inspire reverence, his countenance sufficient to inspire awe, and his words sufficient to be trusted. The 'Punishments of Fu' says: 'Be reverent and cautious, and let there be no words of blame in your person.'" The Master said: "The alternation of baring the chest and covering it with the outer garment is not done without reason; it is to make the people not be disrespectful to one another." The Master said: "In sacrifices, utmost reverence is required, and one should not follow them with pleasure; in audiences at court, utmost discrimination is required, and one should not follow them with weariness." The Master said: "The gentleman is cautious to avoid calamity, sincere so as not to be humiliated, and respectful to keep shame at a distance." The Master said: "The gentleman, being grave and reverent, grows stronger day by day; being at ease and indulgent, he grows lax day by day. The gentleman does not allow himself for a single day to be so remiss as to seem unable to endure the day." The Master said: "One fasts and abstains to serve the spirits and gods, and selects days and months to see the ruler, fearing that the people may not be reverent." The Master said: "Those who are familiar and contemptuous may die and still not be afraid." The Master said: "Without proper words, there is no exchange; without proper rites, there is no meeting; this is to make the people not treat one another with disrespect. The 'Yi' says: 'At the first divination, the answer is given; if repeated two or three times, it is importunate; being importunate, no answer is given.'"
The Master said: "Benevolence is the standard of the world; righteousness is the regulation of the world; requital is the benefit of the world." The Master said: "If one requites kindness with kindness, the people will have encouragement; if one requites resentment with resentment, the people will have warning. The 'Odes' say: 'No word is without response, no virtue is without requital.' The 'Tai Jia' says: 'The people cannot be at peace without the ruler; the ruler cannot govern the four quarters without the people.'" The Master said: "To requite resentment with virtue is the benevolence of one who seeks to preserve his person; to requite virtue with resentment is the conduct of one who deserves punishment." The Master said: "One who loves benevolence without desire, and hates what is not benevolent without fear, is alone in the world. Therefore, the gentleman deliberates on the Way with himself, but establishes laws according to the people." The Master said: "There are three kinds of benevolence, which share the same achievement but differ in feeling. When they share the same achievement, their benevolence cannot yet be known; when they share the same fault, then their benevolence can be known. The benevolent rest in benevolence; the wise profit from benevolence; those who fear guilt force themselves to be benevolent. The benevolent is the right hand; the Way is the left hand. The benevolent is humanity; the Way is righteousness. One who is generous in benevolence but meager in righteousness is loved but not revered; one who is generous in righteousness but meager in benevolence is revered but not loved. The Way has what is perfect, what is righteous, and what is examinable. The perfect Way leads to kingship; the righteous Way leads to hegemony; the examinable Way is to ensure no loss."
The Master said: "Benevolence has degrees, and righteousness has lengths, shortness, greatness, and smallness. Deep compassion and grief in the heart is the benevolence of loving others; following the law and forcing oneself is one who borrows from benevolence. The 'Odes' say: 'The Feng River has its qi grass; did King Wu not employ it! He left plans to his descendants, to secure and protect his sons; how great was King Wu!' This is benevolence for several generations. The 'Airs of the States' say: 'If I am not accepted now, how can I care for those after me?' This is benevolence for one's lifetime." The Master said: "Benevolence as a vessel is heavy, and as a Way it is distant; none who lift it can bear it, and none who walk it can reach it. One who takes much is benevolent; is it not difficult for one who strives at benevolence? Therefore, if the gentleman measures people by righteousness, it is hard to be a person; if he measures people by human standards, then the worthy can be known." The Master said: "One whose heart rests in benevolence is alone in the world. The 'Da Ya' says: 'Virtue is light as a hair, yet few can lift it; I consider it, only Zhong Shan Fu can lift it, and love cannot help him.'" The 'Xiao Ya' says: "The high mountain is looked up to; the great road is traveled." The Master said: "The 'Odes' love benevolence in this way; facing the Way and walking, stopping midway, forgetting the aging of the body, not knowing that years are insufficient, bending down and striving daily, only ceasing at death." The Master said: "The difficulty of achieving benevolence has long existed! Everyone loses what they love; therefore, the faults of the benevolent are easy to excuse." The Master said: "Reverence is near propriety, frugality is near benevolence, sincerity is near feeling; if one acts with respect and yielding, though there may be faults, they will not be great. Reverence leads to few faults, feeling can be trusted, and frugality is easy to manage; is it not rare for one to fail in this way? The 'Odes' say: 'The gentle and reverent man is the foundation of virtue.'" The Master said: "The difficulty of achieving benevolence has long existed; only the gentleman can do it. Therefore, the gentleman does not afflict others with what he himself can do, nor shame others with what they cannot do. Therefore, when the sage establishes conduct, he does not set it by himself, but makes the people have encouragement and shame, to carry out his words. Propriety regulates it, sincerity binds it, appearance adorns it, clothing changes it, friends perfect it, wishing the people to have singleness. The 'Xiao Ya' says: 'Not ashamed before others, not fearing Heaven.' Therefore, the gentleman wears his garments, then adorns them with the gentleman's appearance; having his appearance, he adorns it with the gentleman's speech; fulfilling his speech, he fills it with the gentleman's virtue. Therefore, the gentleman is ashamed to wear his garments without his appearance, ashamed to have his appearance without his speech, ashamed to have his speech without his virtue, ashamed to have his virtue without his conduct. Therefore, when the gentleman wears mourning garments, he has a mournful countenance; when he wears the ceremonial cap and robes, he has a reverent countenance; when he wears armor and helmet, he has a countenance that cannot be disgraced. The 'Odes' say: 'The pelican is on the bridge, not wetting its wings; those recorded ones do not match their garments.'"

zh:
余本庸人，惧死贪生，人之常情。然不该……（中间字样焚毁）妄求长生。
入茧之苦，非人言可述。血肉剥离，筋骨寸断；更何况新躯亦如复燃死灰，终究是已经枯朽之物，老朽之速数倍于常人，不过几度春秋，便又得重遭扒皮换骨之罪。
当初若知是这般滋味，纵再惧死……
蚕母之名，本是余为安信众之心所造。可这谎说了千百遍，到如今夜深独坐时，余竟已分不清。
若蚕母当真有灵……若当真有……
恕余贪妄……
en:
I am only a common man. To fear death and cling to life is human nature. Yet, I never should have... (text burned away) ...so blindly sought immortality.
The agony of the cocoon is beyond words. Flesh is stripped away, and bones and sinews shatter inch by inch. Worse still, the new body is like dead ashes rekindled, rotted at its core. It ages and withers several times faster than a normal man. In just a few short years, I must endure the torment of being skinned and reforged all over again.
Had I known what this would feel like... no matter how much I feared death...
I made up the "Silkworm Mother" to keep the believers in line. But after repeating the lie a thousand times, sitting here alone in the dark... I can no longer tell truth from fiction.
If the Silkworm Mother is truly watching... if she is real...
Forgive my wretched greed...
Dawn Clouds and River

郝闲是陈全从外头捡回来的小孩。
那天下了好大的雨，陈全倒卧于树下饮酒，忽的听闻异响。后他在一个空了的大酒缸里找着一个八九岁的娃娃。那娃娃浑身湿透，蜷缩成一团，瞧着怪可怜的。
陈全心一软，大手一抓，把他揪了出来。结果那娃娃跟没了命似的大喊大叫，不断挣扎。陈全只好松了手。而那娃娃落进酒缸后，竟又安静了下来。好像对那娃娃而言，这整个世界，只有酒缸是最安全的。
陈全守了那酒缸几日，最后带着缸和人，一起回了鬼市子。
en:
Hao Xian was a stray kid Chen Quan took in. 
It was pouring rain that day. Chen Quan was sprawled under a tree, drinking, when he suddenly heard something odd. Following the noise, he found a little boy, maybe eight or nine years old, huddled inside an empty wine vat. The kid was drenched and looked completely miserable. 
Moved by pity, Chen Quan reached in and pulled him out. But the moment he did, the boy started screaming and fighting like his life depended on it. Chen Quan had no choice but to let him go, and the boy immediately climbed back into the vat and fell silent. It seemed like, for him, the wine vat was the only safe place in the world. 
Chen Quan kept an eye on the vat and the boy inside it for a few days, and in the end, he brought both back with him to the Ghostlight Market.

镇戍仓的将士在外头捡回来两猫两狗，自打它们聚首后便整日吵得不可开交，都认为自己对营里功劳最大。
闹闹觉得，整个镇戍仓离了哪只猫猫狗狗都行，可千万离不开它。
原因无它，因为闹闹是一只会报时的小猫。
报时，报食也。近来镇戍仓里的将士们一日忙过一日，人一忙起来，就容易忘掉吃饭。
闹闹觉得这可不行，天大地大，吃饭最大。
所以，每到饭点的时候，闹闹就成了镇戍仓里最严格的监工，若是让它发现谁来不及吃饭，便会一直跟在身后，扯一扯裤脚，再抹一抹自己的嘴巴。
人，再被我抓住忘记吃饭的话，我就要闹了！
en:
The soldiers at the Toilgrain Barn rescued two cats and two dogs. Ever since they gathered, they've been arguing incessantly, each believing they've done the most for the camp.
Fussy thinks that while the Toilgrain Barn could do without any other cat or dog, it absolutely cannot do without her.
The reason is simple: Fussy is a kitten who keeps time.
Keeping time means keeping mealtime. Lately, the soldiers in the Toilgrain Barn have been getting busier by the day, and when people are busy, they tend to forget to eat.
Fussy thinks this won't do; in this great world, eating is the most important thing.
So, at every mealtime, Fussy becomes the strictest supervisor in the Toilgrain Barn. If she finds someone too busy to eat, she follows behind them, tugs at their pant legs, and licks her own lips.
Human, if I catch you forgetting to eat again, I'm going to make a scene!

【成公第八】

元年，春，王正月，公即位。
○二月，辛酉，葬我君宣公。
○无冰。
终时无冰则志。此未终时而言无冰何也？终无冰矣，加之寒之辞也。
○三月，作丘甲。
作，为也，丘为甲也。丘甲，国之事也。丘作甲，非正也。丘作甲之为非正何也？古者，立国家，百官具，农工皆有职以事上。古者，有四民，有士民，有商民，有农民，有工民。夫甲，非人人之所能为也。丘作甲，非正也。
○夏，臧孙许及晋侯盟于赤棘。
○秋，王师败绩于贸戎。
不言战，莫之敢敌也。为尊者讳敌不讳败，为亲者讳败不讳敌，尊尊亲亲之义也。然则孰败之？晋也。
○冬，十月。
季孙行父秃，晋郄克眇，卫孙良夫跛，曹公子手偻，同时聘于齐。齐侯使秃者御秃者，使眇者御眇者，使跛者御跛者，使偻者御偻者。萧同侄子处台上而笑之。闻于客，客不说而去，相与立胥闾而语，移日不解。齐人有知之者曰:"齐之患，必自此始矣。"

二年，春，齐侯伐我北鄙。
○夏，四月，丙戌，卫孙良夫帅师及齐师战于新筑，卫师败绩。
○六月，癸酉，季孙行父、臧孙许、叔孙侨如、公孙婴齐帅师会晋郄克、卫孙良夫、曹公子手，及齐侯战于鞌，齐师败绩。
其日，或曰日其战也，或曰日其悉也。曹无大夫，其曰公子何也？以吾之四大夫在焉，举其贵者也。
○秋，七月，齐侯使国佐如师。乙酉，及国佐盟于爰娄。
鞌，去国五百里。爰娄，去国五十里。一战绵地五百里，焚雍门之茨，侵车东至海。君子闻之曰:"夫甚。"甚之辞焉，齐有以取之也。齐之有以取之何也？败卫师于新筑，侵我北鄙，敖郄献子，齐有以取之也。爰娄在师之外。郄克曰:"反鲁、卫之侵地，以纪侯之甗来，以萧同侄子之母为质，使耕者皆东其亩，然后与子盟。"国佐曰:"反鲁、卫之侵地，以纪侯之甗来，则诺。以萧同侄子之母为质，则是齐侯之母也。齐侯之母，犹晋君之母也，晋君之母犹齐侯之母也。使耕者尽东其亩，则是终士齐也，不可。请一战，一战不克，请再；再不克，请三；三不克，请四；四不克，请五；五不克，举国而授。"于是而与之盟。
○八月，壬午，宋公鲍卒。
○庚寅，卫侯速卒。
○取汶阳田。
○冬，楚师、郑师侵卫。
○十有一月，公会楚公子婴齐于蜀。
楚无大夫，其曰公子何也？婴齐亢也。
○丙申，公及楚人、秦人、宋人、陈人、卫人、郑人、齐人、曹人、邾人、薛人、缯人盟于蜀。
楚其称人何也？于是而后公得其所也。会与盟同月，则地会，不地盟。不同月，则地会地盟。此其地会地盟何也？以公得其所，申其事也。今之屈，向之骄也。

……
en:
【Duke Cheng, Eighth Year】

First Year, Spring, the King's first month, the Duke assumed the throne.
○Second month, Xinyou, we buried our ruler Duke Xuan.
○No ice.
When there is no ice for the entire season, it is recorded. Why does it say "no ice" before the season has ended? Because there will be no ice for the entire season, and this is a word of extreme chill.
○Third month, instituted the "Qiu Jia" (military levy by district).
"Zuo" means to make; the districts were made into armor units. The Qiu Jia is a matter of the state. Making armor by district is not proper. Why is making armor by district not proper? In ancient times, when establishing a state or family, all officials were provided, and farmhands and artisans all had duties to serve their superiors. In ancient times, there were four classes of people: the scholar class, the merchant class, the farmer class, and the artisan class. Now, armor is not something that everyone can make. Making armor by district is not proper.
○Summer, Zang Sun Xu and the Marquis of Jin formed an alliance at Chiji.
○Autumn, the King's army was defeated at Maorong.
It does not say "battle," because no one dared to resist them. For the exalted, one conceals resistance but not defeat; for the close, one conceals defeat but not resistance. This is the principle of honoring the honored and cherishing the cherished. Then who defeated them? Jin did.
○Winter, tenth month.
Ji Sun Xingfu was bald, Jin Que Ke was blind in one eye, Wei Sun Liangfu was lame, and Cao's young master Shou was hunchbacked. They all went to Qi at the same time on a diplomatic mission. The Marquis of Qi had the bald man receive the bald man, the one-eyed man receive the one-eyed man, the lame man receive the lame man, and the hunchbacked man receive the hunchbacked man. Xiao Tong Nizi sat on the terrace and laughed at them. This was heard by the guests, who were displeased and left. They stood together at Xulü and talked, and for days they did not disperse. A man of Qi who knew of this said: "The troubles of Qi will surely begin from this."

Second Year, Spring, the Marquis of Qi attacked our northern border.
○Summer, fourth month, Bingxu, Wei's Sun Liangfu led troops and fought with Qi's army at Xinzhu, and Wei's army was defeated.
○Sixth month, Guiyou, Ji Sun Xingfu, Zang Sun Xu, Shu Sun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led troops to join Jin's Que Ke, Wei's Sun Liangfu, and Cao's young master Shou, and fought with the Marquis of Qi at An, and Qi's army was defeated.
As for the date, some say it records the day of the battle, and some say it records the day of the full mobilization. Cao had no high officials, so why does it say "young master"? Because our four great officers were present, and it elevates the noble ones.
○Autumn, seventh month, the Marquis of Qi sent Guo Zuo to the camp. Yiyou, they formed an alliance with Guo Zuo at Ailou.
An was five hundred li from the capital. Ailou was fifty li from the capital. One battle stretched across five hundred li of land, burned the thatch of the Yong Gate, and the invading chariots reached the sea in the east. The gentleman heard of this and said: "This is extreme." It is a word of extremity, and Qi brought it upon itself. Why did Qi bring it upon itself? It defeated Wei's army at Xinzhu, invaded our northern border, and insulted Que Xianzi. Qi brought it upon itself. Ailou was outside the camp. Que Ke said: "Return the invaded lands of Lu and Wei, offer the Yan of the Marquis of Ji, take Xiao Tong Nizi's mother as a hostage, and make all the farmers till their fields facing east, and then I will form an alliance with you." Guo Zuo said: "Returning the invaded lands of Lu and Wei and offering the Yan of the Marquis of Ji—this I agree to. But taking Xiao Tong Nizi's mother as a hostage—she is the mother of the Marquis of Qi. The mother of the Marquis of Qi is like the mother of the ruler of Jin, and the mother of the ruler of Jin is like the mother of the Marquis of Qi. Making all the farmers till their fields facing east would mean that in the end, the land would belong to Qi. This cannot be done. I request one battle; if one battle is not won, I request a second; if the second is not won, I request a third; if the third is not won, I request a fourth; if the fourth is not won, I request a fifth; if the fifth is not won, I will hand over the entire state." At this, they formed an alliance with him.
○Eighth month, Renwu, Duke Bao of Song died.
○Gengyin, Marquis Su of Wei died.
○Took the fields of Wenyang.
○Winter, the armies of Chu and Zheng invaded Wei.
○Eleventh month, the Duke met with Chu's young master Yingqi at Shu.
Chu had no high officials, so why does it say "young master"? Because Yingqi was arrogant.
○Bingshen, the Duke and the men of Chu, Qin, Song, Chen, Wei, Zheng, Qi, Cao, Zhu, Xue, and Zeng formed an alliance at Shu.
Why does it call the Chu representative "man"? Because it was after this that the Duke achieved his aim. When the meeting and the alliance were in the same month, the place of the meeting is recorded, and the place of the alliance is not. When they were in different months, both the place of the meeting and the place of the alliance are recorded. Why are both the place of the meeting and the place of the alliance recorded here? Because the Duke achieved his aim, and it sets forth the matter fully. The present humiliation is the result of past arrogance.

……

en:
Po, my dear brother:

Learning that you are still alive in this world, I wept tears of absolute joy. Seeing your bearing today, you have truly become the great hero we both envisioned in our youth: every stance and every strike is exactly as we once hoped.
The moment you drew your sword that day, I recognized you... I know not what wondrous encounters you had after escaping the Shengle Sect all those years ago, or if some divine physician altered your features too...
We were born as twin branches, sharing one heart and one face, yet now our paths have split, separated forever like the morning and evening stars.
...Your brother was foolish. Driven by selfish desires, I dared to wear the face of our sworn enemy. Now altered beyond recognition, how could I possibly have the face to meet you!
This letter will never reach your eyes... I only wish for the rest of your life to be smooth and peaceful. Just pretend your brother died in those years past, and think of me no more.
From beneath the yellow springs, I shall pray for you, blessing my little brother with a life free of sorrow.

水煎包
水煎包是胡辣汤最忠诚的护卫。水煎包，相传在东京开封府曾被御赐“二品包子”称号，也不知真是官家起的还是宫人传的。包子并不稀奇，但水煎包最重要的是就是它那一层煎的面壳和焦皮。正是因为这块小小的焦皮，才叫一个软绵的包子有了硬度和嘎嘣脆的口感。这就是为什么拎回家的水煎包不如早起自己去小吃摊上吃好吃。水煎包的这块焦皮要是软了，那吃起来的趣味就要少八成了。
en:
5. Pan-Fried Buns

Pan-fried buns are hulatang's most loyal bodyguard. There's a story that they were once awarded the title "Second-Rank Buns" in Kaifeng, though nobody knows whether it came from the court or just started as palace gossip.

Buns aren't rare. What makes these special is the seared bottom, that thin, browned crust.

That little patch of crisp is what gives a soft, pillowy bun its bite and that satisfying crunch. It's also why pan-fried buns are best eaten right at the stall. Take them home and the crust turns soft, and most of the fun is gone.

Use cold water to wash white salt, let it settle for the clear liquid, add ground pepper, and soak. Take out after two nights and dry in the shade." zh:
……这是随公主出嫁的第五个年头……
今夜雪格外大。公主又命我取来了月奴的思乡酒。
公主从不贪杯，但不知是否因为今夜月色和长安的一样美。
她喝了一杯又一杯，哭得格外伤心。
我亲眼见到她的眼中流出殷红的血泪。但她却似乎并无知觉。
那滴血落入公主手中的簪子，又被她远远抛入湖中。
她摸着我的手，喃喃念着听不真切的唐音。
我知道她想家了。但又能做什么……
我和她的命，不是一样的么。
en:
...It has been five years since I accompanied the princess to her marriage, so far from home.
The snow falls so heavily tonight. She called for me again, to bring Yuenu's Wine of Longing.
The princess is never one for drink, but perhaps tonight the moon reminds her too much of the one that shines over Chang'an. She drank cup after cup, her weeping inconsolable.
I saw it with my own eyes—crimson tears of blood fell from her lashes, though she seemed not to feel them. One drop landed on the hairpin in her hand, just before she flung it far into the dark water.
She clutched my hand, her whispers of the Tang tongue too faint to be understood.
I know she is homesick. But what can I do...?
Is her fate not my own?

我瞧她神气不宁，游魂若絮，三焦气散……为她诊脉时，她告诉我，她经常通夕不寐……觉得己身分而为两，魂魄飞扬离体……
唉，心有远游之愿，却只能困于病榻，也是可怜！
明日当以岐黄之术叩问太素，拟以合魂丹固本，佐独活汤疏郁。
en:
The young lady Duan next door is said to have been recuperating here for a long time, yet she never seems to improve. 
Although I have not lived here long and have only examined her pulse a handful of times... the illness she suffers from is truly rare! In my opinion, it is not caused by exposure to cold or heat, but likely the soul-separation illness! 
I observe her spirit restless, her wandering soul like drifting willow catkins, the qi of her triple burner scattered... When I checked her pulse, she told me she often stays awake all night... feeling as if her body splits in two, her soul flying away from it... 
Alas, her heart longs to travel far, yet she is confined to a sickbed. How pitiable! 
Tomorrow, I shall consult the principles of medicine to question the origins of her constitution, and plan to use a Soul Reviving Pill to strengthen her foundation, aided by Du Huo Decoction to alleviate stagnation.
Here you go! (Why does that sound kind of sarcastic...)

en:
Long bridge through clouded waters, its end beyond sight. A thousand miles over ripples, through all Jiangnan.
The Sleeping Daoist carries his sack on his back while his little donkey ambles along. Misty waters stretch to the horizon, filled with fellow travelers. A wanderer who left home in youth, a warrior gazing north toward the Central Plains, a scholar carrying books and scrolls... Children with dangling hair and elders with hoary brows all seem half unreal in the endless Jiangnan rain, walking near and far along the long bridge. A sudden downpour arrives, fog swallows the way, and oh! Why is the bridge ahead broken? The Daoist stumbles and slowly wakes. He has reached Broken Bridge! The long bridge was never broken. Clear skies shine upon a placid lake, and the Daoist grasps the truth, departing with laughter. The road through mist and water ended in his dream; the road through Jiangnan before his eyes still waits to be traveled.

《重屏会棋图》是五代时期画家周文矩创作的一幅绢本设色人物画，原本已经失佚，现存最早的宋摹本收藏于北京故宫博物院。画中描摹南唐中主李璟与其弟弟们会棋的情景。画中运用“战笔”法，作品构思奇巧，屏风中又画一屏风，也被人们称为“重屏”图，宋代以来有多个摹本。作为带有写实风格的宫廷绘画作品，作者在逼真地刻画出人物肖像特征的同时，也真实地描绘出室内的生活用具，为后人研究五代时期各种生活器用的形制以及中古时期宫廷生活场景提供了重要的形象资料。
现藏于北京故宫博物院。
en:
"The Double-Screen Weiqi Match" is a silk painting created by the Five Dynasties artist Zhou Wenju. Although the original has been lost, the earliest surviving Song Dynasty copy is kept at the Palace Museum in Beijing. The artwork depicts Southern Tang's ruler Li Jing playing go with his brothers. Using the "trembling stroke" technique, the composition is ingeniously designed, featuring a screen within a screen—hence the name "Double Screen." Several copies were made during the Song Dynasty. As a realistic court painting, this work not only vividly captures the likenesses of the figures but also accurately depicts the everyday objects inside the room. This makes it an important visual resource for historians studying household items and palace life during the Five Dynasties and medieval China. 
Today, the painting is preserved at the Palace Museum in Beijing.

zh:
卫璇和娘子也结缘在一次嫖姚棋局中。
嫖姚棋对力道的要求极高，故世人多认为女子难以驾驭。可那一天，连续九胜的卫璇败给了一位温婉的女子。对方明媚聪慧，仿佛灼灼的海棠。
“你这呆子，输了还不快给我彩头。”小娘子展颜一笑，卫璇登时就忘了言语。
后来，三媒六聘，鸿雁成礼。新婚洞房那天，待宾客散去，卫璇和娘子默契地掏出了嫖姚棋，酣战一夜。

世人常说举案齐眉，夫唱妇随。但对卫璇夫妇而人来说，两人是夫妻，是棋友，更是师徒。
卫娘子从小跟随阿爷玩嫖姚棋，尽管力道稍逊，却多在角度上下功夫。她的棋技玄妙多变，常有四两拨千斤之感，是多数男子不能及的招数。卫璇央求娘子教自己几招，得到的也只是娘子的黠然一笑。

没办法，卫璇只得和娘子约好，每日申正，若卫璇回家，卫娘子就要传授嫖姚棋技。对卫娘子来说，申时天色近昏，郎君早点回家也安心，便应承下来。

就这样，卫璇“惧内”的消息就传开了。偶尔卫娘子也会抱怨，说自己千防万防，最后还是因为这嫖姚棋让自己丢了好名儿。卫璇则在一边赧然不语。
“罢，罢，”卫娘子笑出声来。“此中之乐，岂不比贤名更甚？”
en:
Wei Xuan and his wife also met over a game of Piaoyao Battleboard. 
Piaoyao Battleboard demanded great physical strength, so the world mostly believed women couldn't master it. But that day, Wei Xuan, on a nine-win streak, was defeated by a gentle woman. She was bright and clever, like a blazing crabapple flower. 
"You fool, you lost. Hurry up with my prize." The young woman smiled, and Wei Xuan was instantly speechless. 
Later came endless efforts for their marriage. On their wedding night, after the guests had gone, Wei Xuan and his wife wordlessly took out the Piaoyao Battleboard set and battled delightedly until dawn. 

The world often spoke of mutual respect, of the husband leading and the wife following. But for the Wei couple, they were husband and wife, chess partners, and also teacher and student. 
Madam Wei had played Piaoyao Battleboard with her father since childhood. Though slightly weaker in strength, she excelled in angles and strategy, often achieving much with little—moves most men couldn't match. Wei Xuan begged his wife to teach him a few tricks, only to be met with her sly smile. 

Left with no choice, Wei Xuan made a pact with his wife: every day at four in the afternoon, if he was home, Madam Wei would instruct him in Piaoyao Battleboard. For Madam Wei, dusk was near by then, and having her husband home early was reassuring, so she agreed. 

Thus, the news of Wei Xuan being "henpecked" spread. Occasionally, Madam Wei would complain, saying she had guarded against everything, yet in the end, it was this Piaoyao Battleboard that had ruined her good name. Wei Xuan would just blush silently beside her. 
"Ah, forget it," Madam Wei would laugh. "The joy within this... isn't it greater than a spotless reputation?"

zh:
阳光正好，梨花又飘。午后的天光从竹叶罅隙中漏下，洒做碎金。暖洋洋的风像猫狸子，轻轻挠抓搔你的脸。十六岁离家后，你鲜少回到这里。檐下的蛛网结成画，屋子的主人去了天涯。你坐在昔日他坐着的长椅上，想起曾经自己的童言稚语，缓缓入睡。
恍惚间，你睁开眼，竟看到江叔牵着一匹马，向你走来。印象中的江叔背脊永远这般笔直，宽阔的肩膀如山如岗，为你挡下风雨。可如今你却发现他的衣摆有些脏了，脸上似乎也有了微不可察的疲惫。
此刻你有千言万语想说，但还未及开口，他便抬手止住。他似是猜到你所想，只微颔首，开口询问：
即便如此，你也想入江湖？
看着他的眼睛，你脱口而出——
⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛⬛
听见你的回答，江叔点点头。他的眼神并没有什么波动，仿佛你的回答正如他所预料。在他的面前，你可以畅所欲言。因为你知道，不管你的选择是什么，他永远都站在你的身后。曾经，你是他怀中熟睡的婴孩，是他与这个世界的纽系。未来，你会成为他的骄傲，或是牵挂吗。
你起身奔向江叔，想要问问他去了哪里，问问他过得好不好。倏忽间，你的腿抽动了一下，撞在了桌角——疼痛让你睁开了眼。
阳光依然好，梨花还在飘。天光撒做碎金。风里没有故人的消息，但又处处是他，和他们的消息。
en:
The sun shines bright, and pear blossoms drift down once more. Afternoon light filters through the bamboo leaves, scattering like flecks of gold. A warm breeze, soft as a cat's paw, gently teases your cheek. You have seldom returned since leaving home at sixteen. Cobwebs beneath the eaves have woven into intricate paintings, while the master of the house has wandered to the ends of the earth. Sitting on the long bench where he once sat, you recall your childish prattle from long ago and slowly drift off to sleep.
In a daze, you open your eyes, only to see Uncle Jiang leading a horse toward you. In your memory, Uncle Jiang's back is forever straight, his broad shoulders like a sturdy mountain sheltering you from the wind and rain. Yet now, you notice his hem is slightly soiled, and a barely perceptible weariness lingers on his face.
Thousands of words rush to your lips, but before you can even speak, he raises a hand to stop you. As if guessing your thoughts, he gives a slight nod and asks:
"Even so, do you still wish to wander in the jianghu?"

Meeting his gaze, you blurt out...

Hearing your answer, Uncle Jiang nods. His gaze remains steady, as if your response is exactly as he expected. Before him, you can always speak your mind. For you know that no matter your choice, he will always stand behind you. Once, you were a sleeping infant in his arms, his tether to this world. In the future, will you become his pride, or his lingering worry?
You rise and run toward Uncle Jiang, curious about where he has been and whether he has been well. Suddenly, your leg twitches, striking the corner of the table. The pain jolts your eyes open.
The sun remains bright, and the pear blossoms keep drifting down. The daylight scatters like flecks of gold. The wind carries no news of old friends, yet traces of him, and of them all, can be found everywhere.

zh:
地下沟渠阴晦潮湿，脏污遍地，令人闻之胆寒，普通人避之不及。
但它却是刘庄的家。

这个怪老头佝偻着背，蹒跚着走过沟渠许多地方，找来许多别人弃如敝履之物，堆放在洞穴里，给自己搭建了一个家。
然后他蜷缩着躲在这。目之所及，无来日，亦无过往。
唯有每次敲击编钟的时候，刘庄会想起一些曾经。
那是很辉煌、很骄傲、很美好的曾经。
可惜历史的年轮一层层碾过。他的身份没了，他的爱人没了，他的家人没了，他的信仰没了……
到而今，就剩这么一条行将凋零的性命。

但也正是这条行将凋零的性命，佝偻着背，蹒跚着，为那些在沟渠深处逃亡的迷途者，指引了生路。
迷途者挣脱无忧帮的爪牙，循着钟声而来。他们钻过那小小的口子，跨过生与死的界限，奔赴光明的未来。
而敲钟者日夜守在沟渠的出口，一次次敲击编钟。他以钟声为信，搭起生与死的桥梁，而后目送他们远去。

去找你们的家吧。
刘庄心想。
我的过去，我的当下，我的未来，都已被摧毁。但你们没有。
在一切还有希望的时候，在一切还来得及的时候，离开这里，去搭建一个美丽、温暖的家吧。
这是我想给你们的，最好的祝愿。
en:
The underground sewers were dark, damp, and reeking of filth, a place that struck fear into ordinary hearts, where no sane person would venture.
Yet to Liu Zhuang, this was home.

The hunched old man shuffled through the tunnels, gathering what others had discarded as worthless, piling them in a hollowed-out nook to fashion himself a dwelling.
There he crouched, trapped in a timeless void, no past, no future, only the present stench of decay.
But when he struck his bronze chimes, fragments of a brighter life flickered back.
Glory, pride, love... all now lost to the crushing wheels of history. His status, his lover, his family, his faith, all torn away. 
Until nothing remained but this flickering life, clinging to the edge of extinction.

And yet, it was this very same dying life, this bent-backed, limping wreck of a man, who pointed the way for those lost souls fleeing through the sewers.
Escaping the clutches of the Unbound Cavern, they followed the sound of the chimes. Squeezed through narrow passages. Crossed the boundary between death and life. Ran toward the light.
And the bell-ringer stood watch at the sewer's exit, striking his chimes day and night. With each toll, he built a bridge between the living and the dead, then watched as they vanished into the distance.

Go find your home.
Liu Zhuang thought.
My past, present, and future are dust. But yours aren't.
While there is still hope... while there is still time... leave this place. Build a home full of warmth and light.
This is the last, best gift I can give you.

“报！堂主，今日堂内点卯三百六十二，又少了三人！”
“报！堂主，堂内还剩米粮六十二带，还能撑十六日！”
“报——”
冯如之翻着眼前的册页，听着糟心的来信，只是微微点了点头。比“不在乎”更恐怖的，是“习惯”：先习惯日复一日的坏消息，再习惯没米没面的土灶，最后习惯水来土掩的命。
黄河边的人，似乎生来便是为了习惯。习惯了弯腰，所以纤绳被牢牢勒在肩膀的皮肉上；习惯了面朝黄土，所以脊梁就被牢牢钉在了瓠子坝上。
可黄河边的人，从来不习惯端着饭碗，还要看天吃饭；不习惯跳进水里，洗不清一身冤；不习惯顶天的脊梁，被世道硬生生敲断。一切习惯，只为了等一次“不习惯”，一次与天争命，绝不低头的“不习惯”。
“报！堂主！白马驿有消息，说是冯老大要回来了！”
“知道了。”
en:
"Report! Hall Master, three hundred sixty-two answered roll call today. Three fewer than yesterday!"
"Report! Hall Master, we have sixty-two sacks of grain left. Enough for sixteen more days!"
"Report!"
Feng Ruzhi flips through the pages in front of him, and pauses over yet another disheartening letter. He merely nods; not because he doesn't care, but because he's grown used to it all: first the daily toll of bad news, then cooking over a mud stove with no rice or flour, and finally, swallowing whatever the world throws at him, taking calamity as routine.
The people who live by the Yellow River seem born to endure. Born to bend, so the ropes bite deep into the shoulders that carry them. Born to face the earth, so their backs hunch low like staples hammered into the dam.
But there are things they never learn to live with: Holding their own bowls while still begging the sky for rain. Jumping into the river and expecting it to wash away blame. Standing tall, only for the world to break their backs. Every act of endurance is just waiting for a moment they stop enduring. The moment they defy the heavens, and refuse to kneel.
"Report! Hall Master! There's word from Baima Station. Boss Feng is coming back!"
"... Got it."

天真——要将这二字落在纸上，只消笔尖吸上几口墨色，画下寥寥数道，一张轻薄纸，一阙风流词，便足以承它处处天真词汇。
可这天真二字，一旦落在人的身上，便比千金更重，比赤铁更沉，使人行也不能，逃也吃力，哭也无声，叹也惹笑，直到被这二字扼死在乱世之中，众人从这被天真扼死的尸首旁走过，十人之中，五人嘲弄，三人叹惋，二人怒骂。
你说这轻重之间，岂不是天大的怪事？
秦弱兰见过不少因天真而死的人，听过太多从那些尸首旁走过的闲言碎语。
那这一个呢？
她利用$N，拿到了所要之物，利用人的是她，但不愿人死的也是她。
那史书纸笔之上的天真二字，又何曾是墨色，那墨色之下究竟埋着几个人，藏着几丝血色？
她见过了千金，知道这落在人身上的天真，比千金更重，却也比千金更贵。
贵到她在某些间隙亦开始担忧，这人也会成为血色之一吗？秦弱兰垂眸翻过纸上的天真二字，抚去那失神落下的墨滴。
en:
"Innocence"—if you wrote it out, it'd take just a few strokes of ink on a thin sheet of paper, a few lines in a poem, light and delicate, and that would be enough to capture the word's gentle meaning.
But in real life, innocence is heavier than gold, heavier than iron. It can keep you from moving forward, make it hard to run away, make your tears silent, your sighs absurd until it finally strangles you in the chaos of the world. And when people walk past the body, five out of ten will mock, three will sigh, and two will curse.
Isn't it strange how something so light could be so heavy?
Qin Ruolan had seen many people die because of their innocence, and heard too many whispers around their graves.
And what about this one?
She'd used $N to get what she wanted; she was the one who used people, yet she didn't want them to die.
That word, "innocence," written in ink in the history books, was it ever just ink? How many people's stories are buried under that black? How many traces of blood are hidden beneath the words?
She'd seen wealth and known that innocence, when it falls on a person, is heavier than gold, and yet, more precious too.
So precious that sometimes, Qin Ruolan found herself worrying. Would this person, too, become just one more spot of blood? She lowered her eyes, brushed away the stray drop of ink that had fallen onto the word "innocence" in her book.
